extracted.intended_audience: Sage developers and documentation authors (people writing Sage manuals using Sphinx/reStructuredText)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural rules for authoring, building, linking, and testing Sage manuals written in reStructuredText and generated with Sphinx. Covers file locations, build commands, cross-references, doctests, and special Sage roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reStructuredText and Sphinx
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage’s manuals are written in ReST (reStructuredText), and generated with the software Sphinx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documentation content should be authored in reStructuredText so it can be built with Sphinx. The developer guide and other manuals assume ReST/Sphinx workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual file locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manual lives under SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/<name> (e.g. tutorial, developer, constructions, installation, reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/tutorial, SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/developer, SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/constructions, SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/installation, SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference. More specialized manuals also appear under SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en. Translated documents use other language codes under the same tree (fr/, es/, de/, ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Build HTML with sage --docbuild
rubrics_metrics.description: To visualize edited documents, build an HTML version with sage --docbuild <document> html.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: $ sage --docbuild tutorial html. After building you can open SAGE_ROOT/local/share/doc/sage/html/en/tutorial/index.html in a browser. See the 'Building the manuals' section for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: All documentation files must pass doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Run automated doctests for documentation — all files must pass tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After modifying documents (e.g. tutorial) run tests with: $ sage -tp SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/tutorial/ . See 'Running automated doctests' for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference manual changes may require building Sage
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the reference manual is mostly generated from Sage source code, you may need to build Sage to see documentation changes for functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To update reference documentation run: $ sage -b && sage --docbuild reference html. Building the code is necessary for docstrings generated from the code to reflect changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Sphinx cross-reference roles for code objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Sphinx roles like :mod:, :class:, :meth:, :func: to create links to modules, classes, methods, and functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: :mod:`link to a module <sage.module_name>`, :mod:`sage.module_name`. Replace :mod: with :class:, :meth:, or :func: for classes, methods, or functions respectively. See Sphinx documentation on cross-referencing Python objects and roles for full syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short cross-reference names with ~
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the leading ~ in a role to display only the final name (short link text) instead of the full dotted path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: :func:`~sage.mod1.mod2.mod3.func1` is equivalent to :func:`func1 <sage.mod1.mod2.mod3.func1>`; the function’s name will be used as the link name instead of its full path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local names allowed for methods within same class
rubrics_metrics.description: When documenting methods of the same class you may use short/local names for links without full qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documenting method_one, you can write :meth:`method_two` to link to another method in the same class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersphinx references for external packages and C constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can refer to modules, classes, methods, and functions of the Python standard library and several packages used by Sage via intersphinx; you can also refer to C functions of libraries like FLINT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Intersphinx documentation for configuration. To inspect available cross references you can run: ./sage-python -m sphinx.ext.intersphinx src/doc/common/_vendor/numpy.inv .

rubrics_metrics.name: Link objects auto-imported into Sage global namespace without full path
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects that are automatically imported by Sage (e.g. integral) can be referenced without their full path in cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: :func:`A link toward the integral function <integral>` — you may omit the full module path for automatically imported objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Sage-specific roles for project-specific references
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage defines roles for linking to issues, repository files, Wikipedia, arXiv, OEIS, DOIs, MathSciNet, and various package-specific targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: :issue:`17596` (GitHub issue), :sage_root:`src/doc/en` (repo file/directory), :wikipedia:`Sage_(mathematics_software)`, :arxiv:`1202.1506`, :oeis:`A000081`, :doi:`10.2752/...`, :mathscinet:`MR0100971`, and other package-specific roles (e.g., :gap:, :pari:, :giac_us:). Use these roles to produce consistent, project-aware links.

rubrics_metrics.name: HTTP links and explicit link text
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy/pasting an http link works directly; to specify link text use the explicit link syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want a specific link name, use: `link name <http://www.example.com>`_. Plain URLs also work, but explicit syntax lets you choose displayed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid duplicate explicit target names; prefer anonymous hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a single underscore creates an explicit target name which must be unique on the page; duplicates cause Sphinx warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example warning: WARNING: Duplicate explicit target name: ... To avoid the issue either change target names to be different or use anonymous hyperlinks with two underscores: `this page <http://...>`__ .

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting and handling broken links
rubrics_metrics.description: Sphinx can report broken links; use the --warn-links flag to have the build report them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run: $ sage --docbuild --warn-links reference html. Note: Sphinx will not rebuild a document that has not been updated, so it may not report broken links in unchanged files unless they are rebuilt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include new code files in reference manual index
rubrics_metrics.description: If you add a new Sage source file and want its content to appear in the reference manual, add its name to the appropriate index file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add the module name to SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference/<package>/index.rst (replace 'matroids' with your package). For combinat/ subdirectories, add your file to the __init__.py index in that directory and to SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference/combinat/module_list.rst (special procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: sage --docbuild script usage and help
rubrics_metrics.description: All Sage manuals are built using the sage --docbuild script, a thin wrapper around sphinx-build; the general form is sage --docbuild <document-name> <format>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of the script is in SAGE_ROOT/src/sage_docbuild/__init__.py. Example: $ sage --docbuild reference html. Use $ sage --docbuild -h for short help and $ sage --docbuild -H for comprehensive help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphinx output formats are supported
rubrics_metrics.description: All output formats supported by Sphinx (e.g., pdf) can be used in Sage documentation builds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See http://www.sphinx-doc.org/builders.html for the list of builders and formats; pass the desired format as the second argument to sage --docbuild.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document-name convention: lang/name
rubrics_metrics.description: The <document-name> argument to the build command uses the form lang/name where lang is a two-letter language code and name is the descriptive name of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the language is omitted it defaults to English (en). Examples: $ sage --docbuild tutorial html is equivalent to $ sage --docbuild en/tutorial html. To build the French version use: $ sage --docbuild fr/tutorial html .

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax highlighting for Cython code
rubrics_metrics.description: To write Cython code in a ReST file, use code-block or HIGHLIGHT directives for Cython.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede code blocks with: .. CODE-BLOCK:: cython instead of the usual :: . To enable syntax-highlighting for an entire file use: .. HIGHLIGHT:: cython . Example code block is shown in the guide.
